governance.statement: This manifest defines benchmark lanes and data-admission requirements. It does not authorize data ingestion, training, publication of examples, or capability promotion.

candidate_sources.note: Current card reports 64.26h / 18 languages / CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 / gated access; pin immutable revision and rights.
Current card reports 24 languages / 10 domains and evaluation-only intended use; aggregates multiple sources; do not train.

Current HF README revision c247482 reports 54.41h / 16,602 / 73,486 / 14 configurations / one test split / CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Current page exposes direct downloads and independent catalogue reports open access, differing from an earlier gated-status observation. Paper reports 61.36h / 18,861 / 78,333 / 16 varieties / CC BY 4.0. Preserve both snapshots; recheck current access and exact rights. Not a training set because only test split is released.

The 2026 switch-aware study audits 8,181 audio-available rows / 9.54h from 9,966 AfriCodeSwitch validation metadata rows and uses a deterministic 2,000-utterance manifest. Its exact artifact, manifest, license, speaker split and permission must be pinned before use; no download or ingestion is authorized.

~120h / 99,930 validated audio-text pairs / 140 Nigerian bilingual speakers; word-level language tags; tone/sub-dot marked Yoruba; 16 domains. NOODL-1.0: commercial entities headquartered in developed/high-income nations require a benefit-sharing agreement; speaker identification and individual voice cloning prohibited; test audio-only with labels held by steward; access request. Potential training/validation only after exact terms, access, purpose and #10942 admission.

87 consented utterances / 8 speakers / 8.75min across four African-language-English pairs; word tags and gold intent/slot labels; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Card says too small to train or rank systems; read speech, headset-only, Hausa n=9 effectively one speaker; one flagged accidental real-person-name collision requires exclusion or source-owner re-record. Use as smoke test/qualitative slot probe only.
210 Yoruba-English clips with references and outputs from five systems; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; source rows identify AfriSwitch. Use for scorer/output reproduction only, not as an independent test cohort.

tracks.name: Audio-grounded semantic extraction and spoken QA

candidate_sources.note: Entity/number flags are strata, not complete semantic gold; independently adjudicated audio-grounded references required.

Includes gold intent/slot labels and per-token language tags for 87 consented clips. Too small to rank systems and has documented speaker/device/read-speech limitations; one flagged accidental real-person-name collision needs source-owner resolution.

tracks.name: Namibian click-language acoustic and phonetic perception

candidate_sources.note: Current card describes 141 language configurations with 70 native, 13 equivalent and 58 donor rule mappings; Damara is explicitly excluded because click-letter orthography is unsupported. Rule-based IPA reflects orthography, not actual pronunciation. Do not treat donor mappings as expert acoustic gold or infer click coverage for Namibian languages.

tracks.name: Active data selection and low-resource adaptation
tracks.note: Only execute budgets supported by admitted data. Paza's published saturation/efficiency observations are hypotheses to test, not universal thresholds. Include 150/300/400-hour arms when admitted language data supports them, reflecting Paza's published scaling range; this is a test grid, not a universal saturation claim.

candidate_sources.note: Potential admitted Yoruba-English low-resource adaptation source (~120h / 99,930 pairs). NOODL-1.0 restrictions and benefit-sharing apply; public test is audio-only and steward labels are held back. Use train/validation only after rights and governance admission; do not claim the hidden test can be scored locally.

tracks.name: Phonetic supervision provenance and G2P tier audit

candidate_sources.note: Current card says 141 configs: 70 native, 13 equivalent-code, 58 donor; Damara excluded due unsupported click-letter orthography. It warns rule-based IPA reflects orthography, not speaker pronunciation, and donor character coverage does not prove phonological correctness.

tracks.name: Depth-aware multilingual speech adaptation and retention
tracks.note: DAMA (Findings ACL 2026) reports depth-aware adaptation, 80% fewer trainable parameters and 29% error reduction in its own setting. Reproduce on matched South African data/compute; published gains are not assumed to transfer. Add PUMA's Universal Language Projection as a mandatory matched-compute comparator against HDC-conditioned projection; paper gains are not assumed to transfer. Paper: https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.17/.

tracks.name: Cross-implementation metric vector conformance

candidate_sources.note: Ten hand-computed synthetic vectors for WER, PIER, SETER, SPER@k and per-language masked error; schema at voice_metric_vectors_v1.schema.json. Current custom formula/alignment audit passes; this is not Rust execution or cross-implementation differential qualification.

Six synthetic reference/predicted language-tag sequences for exact switch-boundary TP/FP/FN/precision/recall/F1. Independent formula audit recomputes all six cases successfully. This is not language identification evaluation or model output.
Nine synthetic reference/predicted tag sequences for exact boundary position + source-language + destination-language tuple matching. Separate from position-only boundary F1.

tracks.note: All scorer implementations should consume identical frozen vectors. Validate metric counts and denominators separately from floating-point presentation; real-corpus results require additional independent evidence.

tracks.name: Reproducible benchmark experiment receipts

candidate_sources.note: Synthetic example only; no audio, model, benchmark execution or claim.

tracks.note: A leaderboard result without immutable inputs, model/decode/scorer revisions, data admission, split integrity, denominators, clustered uncertainty and efficiency measures is not reproducible evidence. Schema validity is not proof that the recorded facts are true.

tracks.name: Closed-set acoustic transcript hypothesis selection

candidate_sources.note: Findings ACL 2026 evaluates Phi-4 and Qwen3-Omni on three endangered languages; reports multimodal in-context learning, cross-lingual transfer and acoustic-hypothesis selection. No transfer claim to African language cohorts without matched replication.
SAMA-ASR conditions decoding with translation-derived semantic embeddings plus acoustic anchor. This is not candidate selection; compare separately with acoustic-veto controls under #11104.

tracks.note: Candidate selection is not transcript correction. Oracle best-in-pool is an upper bound only. MICL published results are not assumed to transfer to African speech.

tracks.name: Language-profiled phonological feature and tone-aware ASR evaluation

candidate_sources.note: Chen, Adeleke & Downey (AfricaNLP 2026) introduce NA-masked FER and tone-only TER with sparse {-1,0,+1} vectors and Needleman-Wunsch alignment. Their 24-dim inventory is designed for Edoid/Yoruboid phonology; do not apply it to other languages without a native-authorized profile.

tracks.name: Acoustic faithfulness under text, context and prompt conflict

candidate_sources.note: Over 2,700 conflict stimuli covering emotional prosody, background sounds and speaker identity, with staged semantic-context and misleading-prompt conflicts. Evaluate the official protocol; do not assume all tasks or speaker attributes are appropriate for this speech program.

Over 5,000 human-verified audio QA pairs spanning speech, environmental sound and music; reports hallucination, yes/no bias, error types and refusal. Use speech-relevant subsets and pin exact rights/version.

Uses AudioRatio, AudioConsistency, AudioEntropy and TextEntropy attention-derived features with lightweight classifiers. Model-dependent and task-specific; requires attention access and should not be treated as universal confidence.

ParaSpeechRAG (EMNLP 2026) studies semantic stability under speaker, emotion/prosody, noise, speaking-rate and codec perturbations. It is a speech-retrieval robustness comparator, not an ASR benchmark reproduction. Treat speaker identity as nuisance for transcript semantics but as task evidence for diarization/speaker attribution.

tracks.note: Binary evidence_span_present is retained only as a coarse trial-level coverage diagnostic. Confirmatory localization uses the exact evaluation-audio SHA-256 and half-open sample coordinate system from #11218/#11220; the cohort derivation manifest separately maps any transformed evaluation waveform back to its original source. Claim correctness and citation quality remain separate; the scorer does not prove model-internal reliance.

tracks.name: Paired counterfactual nuisance invariance and acoustic evidence sensitivity

candidate_sources.note: AHA identifies event omission, false event identity, temporal relation error and quantitative temporal error; uses counterfactual hard negatives and a separate human-verified evaluation set. Its reported Qwen2.5-Omni gains are author-reported for its evaluated audio reasoning tasks, not African speech or Symthaea.

DEAF varies textual influence over acoustic conflicts. The paired scorer extends this idea with explicit text-nuisance invariance and waveform-relevant sensitivity; do not treat this as an official DEAF reproduction.

ParaSpeechRAG (EMNLP 2026) studies semantic stability under speaker, emotion/prosody, noise, speaking-rate and codec perturbations. It is a speech-retrieval robustness comparator, not an ASR benchmark reproduction. Treat speaker identity as nuisance for transcript semantics but as task evidence for diarization/speaker attribution.

tracks.note: undefined Task-relative extension: acoustic dimensions are not globally nuisance/relevant. Each confirmatory pair must pin target task, ontology revision, acoustic dimension and expected invariant/sensitive/conditional relation; see #11200. These task-relative semantics are a research contract, not yet implemented by the v0.1 pair scorer.

test_vector_sets.note: Token-level synthetic vectors; expected values are formula-checked using the declared deterministic Levenshtein tie-break, but no Rust test, RapidFuzz differential or real-data result is claimed.
Six synthetic token-aligned language-tag cases with exact-position boundary matching; no tolerance and no audio evidence.

Ten synthetic generic feature-profile vectors. A separate JavaScript implementation recomputed FER/TER, NA-aware alignment, and all 40 per-dimension diagnostic rows with no mismatches. This is arithmetic fixture validation only; no Rust tests or external-reference differential have been executed.

Ten synthetic trial groups. Independent JavaScript recomputation of every numerator, denominator and rate matches all expected values; this is formula audit only, not Rust execution or DEAF/HalluAudio reproduction.

Eight synthetic pair-level vectors. Independent JS recomputation of all defined pair numerators/denominators/rates matched after correcting the one-pair denominator for false invariance. No Rust execution or real-audio evaluation.

Nine synthetic cases plus three rejected controls. A separately written JS recomputation matched all declared counts, denominators and rates. This checks arithmetic/fixture consistency only; Rust tests, JSON Schema meta-validation, audio or model execution are not claimed.
